archetype: BG -1/-1 counter aristocrats. deck-audit takes the frame's `combo` archetype and applies its overrides (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6); the deck meets both, at 8 tutors and 5 protection. But the measured behaviour is a converter engine, not a combo deck: 25 creatures, modal mana value 2, a 67.2% commander-plus-payoff assembly, and a headline kill that assembles 16.3% of the time. The frame's own line — 'a genuine but narrow combo ceiling sits above a grindy median' — is what the numbers show.
verdict: This deck starts better than almost anything in the fleet: 36 land copies, zero unconditional taplands, 15 colour sources above Karsten's worst-colour target, a 90.2% turn-3 land drop and a commander on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs. Its payoff class (6), converter class (4) and tutor class (8) are all deep. What binds is the class no axis measures: a repeatable -1/-1 counter SOURCE. Three of the six cards in deck-audit's payoff component — Nest of Scarabs, Flourishing Defenses and Obelisk Spider — do nothing at all until a counter is placed, and Hapatra's own token half is gated the same way; the other three drain on any death and run off a plain sacrifice. Free, repeatable and non-combat, the deck holds two sources: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician without limit, and Devoted Druid for exactly two placements before it kills itself. Both of the audit's flagged single points of failure are one card at 7.1% of an opening seven. Second, and compounding it: the engine is entirely creature activated abilities and the deck answers one permanent class.

add_candidates.why: The correction that matters. I had claimed the class could not be deepened; the deck's own candidate_pool.json refutes that, listing at least nine in-identity repeatable placers, and this is the cheapest of them at {2}{B}. 'At the beginning of your end step, draw a card and blight 1' is a free, repeatable, non-combat source that also draws a card every turn — the pool scores it 0.815 similarity, the highest of the nine, and files it draw:engine + removal:debuff for exactly that reason. The pool's own rules note settles the trigger: self-blight ('put a -1/-1 counter on a creature you control') satisfies Hapatra's 'you put', unlike High Perfect Morcant's opponent-blight. With Hapatra out it is body-neutral — blight a Snake, mint a Snake — while turning on Blowfly Infestation, the drains, Grim Haruspex and Morbid Opportunist. It is a 0/4, so it can absorb its own blight three times if the board is empty. The alternatives, judged rather than ignored: Harbinger of Night ({2}{B}{B}) and Midnight Banshee ({3}{B}{B}{B}) are larger but symmetric and eat your own tokens every upkeep, Persistent Constrictor ({4}{B}) is opponent-facing and doubles as removal but costs five, and Glistening Oil ({B}{B}) is cheapest of all but places only one counter a turn on a single creature. Gnarlbark does NOT win on cost: Glistening Oil is a mana cheaper and Gnarlbark is second of the nine at mana value 3. It wins on the card it draws — it is the only one of the nine the pool files draw:engine, so the only one that also touches card-advantage, the other axis reading under target — and on being body-neutral, since it picks a fresh target each end step instead of consuming the one creature it is attached to.

open_questions.question: Does the Blowfly family loop? Blowfly Infestation paired with Hapatra, with Nest of Scarabs, and with Flourishing Defenses are three of the nineteen claimed two-card infinites, and the pairing with Hapatra is the deck's declared headline kill that goldfish measures at 16.3%. No stack artifact touches any of them. A scenario must settle whether the loop is optional enough to avoid a draw, whether it needs a seed counter and a spare body, and what happens when no legal target remains.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single thinnest declared component in the deck and its status is unknown. A pilot is currently being asked to mulligan toward a line nobody has adjudicated.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus, the Unhallowed switch the token loops OFF? His anthem makes non-Human tokens — Snakes, Insects, Elf Warriors — 2/2, so a single -1/-1 counter no longer takes them to 0 toughness. If that holds, the deck's two flagship engines are mutually exclusive on the battlefield.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether Mikaeus is a combo piece or an anti-synergy, and therefore whether a six-mana single point of failure belongs in a deck whose modal mana value is 2. Stack 001 step 15 already showed his anthem changes exactly this arithmetic for Walking Ballista.

open_questions.question: Does the Ivy Lane family work? Scurry Oak + Ivy Lane Denizen is bracket_report's highest-bracket line, and six further entries pair Ivy Lane with a sacrifice outlet that makes no green creature enter. Verify the Scurry Oak pairing; audit the other six.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Seven of the eleven unadjudicated lines sit here, and the Scurry Oak cut proposed above should not be applied until this returns.

open_questions.question: Does Yawgmoth + Hapatra loop without Mikaeus, and what bounds it? Sacrifice a Snake, place the counter on a creature that survives it, Hapatra mints a replacement Snake — net body count flat, one card drawn and one life paid per activation.
open_questions.why_it_matters: On the evidence this is the line the deck actually wins with most often, it needs neither of the six-mana pieces, and it has never been resolved. Stack 001 verified Yawgmoth's mechanics only inside the Mikaeus line.

open_questions.question: Should goldfish_targets.json declare a counter-SOURCE component, and should the 'Mikaeus + a free sacrifice outlet' target be retired? All five outlets in that target's any_of group — Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Blasting Station — are on stack 001's refuted list, so the simulation is measuring the assembly rate of a line the deck's own verified artifact says does not loop.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Until a source component is declared, the engine block cannot see the class that binds this deck, and the 9.5% figure it does report describes a kill that is not there.

open_questions.question: The corpus has no section on auditing a combo list — how to price a graph-listed two-card infinite against a verified line — and none on the aristocrats outlet/fodder/converter taxonomy or on -1/-1 counters as removal that pays you.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every card-level judgment in this diagnosis about free versus costed outlets, and about counter annihilation as an anti-synergy, had to be derived from oracle text and one stack artifact rather than cited.

Every add above is argued from this deck's own artifacts; a recon pass would tell us whether the source class is thin by choice or by oversight.

CORRECTED from the previous iteration, which asserted that the in-colour pool held no second free repeatable non-combat source. It does. candidate_pool.json names Sinister Gnarlbark, Harbinger of Night, Midnight Banshee, Persistent Constrictor, Glistening Oil, Carnifex Demon, Contagion Engine, Soul Snuffers and Grim Poppet, each with a 'you put -1/-1 counters -> Hapatra snake trigger' note; its WEAKEST BUCKET note lists the sweeper subset by name. What remains genuinely unknown is which of them survives contact with the deck's own tokens — every mass placer is symmetric — and that is a goldfish and a resolve-stack question, not an absence.

deck-audit emits no axis for the counter-source class, so the constraint this diagnosis names as binding is invisible to all sixteen numbers. It is derived from the goldfish any_of groups plus oracle text plus stack 001, not measured.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256 (freshness reports it as unstamped), so its 19-infinite figure and its Game Changer list are not pinned to the current list the way goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json are.
The audit's engine schema cannot express the UNION of independent kills, so there is no single assembled_rate for 'this deck wins'. The 16.3% and 9.5% figures are per-line and must not be added.

Necroskitter is invisible to the role taxonomy: candidate_pool.json records the bug ('recursion requires a graveyard phrase'), so the card carries threat:body only and appears in no axis count, despite being a 1/4 wither blocker that places -1/-1 counters on what it blocks. An axis count is a floor and this is the clearest instance of it in this deck.

findings.note: The Sinister Gnarlbark case names three decision criteria and one of them is false, refuted inside the same field. It opens 'this is the cheapest of them at {2}{B}' and closes 'Gnarlbark wins on cost, on drawing a card, and on being the only one of the nine the pool files draw:engine' - but three sentences earlier it says 'Glistening Oil ({B}{B}) is cheapest of all'. cards.csv: Glistening Oil {B}{B} cmc 2, Sinister Gnarlbark {2}{B} cmc 3. Gnarlbark does not win on cost; it loses to the alternative the entry itself names. The other two criteria hold (I verified Gnarlbark is the only one of the nine with draw:engine, and its 0.815 pool similarity is the highest of the nine), so the add survives on a two-legged argument - but a reader comparing the nine is handed a false tiebreak. Corroborating, same sweep: engine.single_points_of_failure[0] calls the nine 'in-identity cards that place -1/-1 counters repeatably' and lists Soul Snuffers among the closers, whose entire text is 'When this creature enters, put a -1/-1 counter on each creature' - a pure ETB one-shot, filed value:etb in the pool's own roles.
